sources.title: Egypt's First Biennial Transparency Report
sources.organization: Government of Egypt, Ministry of Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical hazards and 2024 baseline, with adaptation plans and projections to 2100.
sources.methodology: Government submission synthesizing climate vulnerability, hazard history and adaptation reporting.
sources.limitations: Some measures and beneficiaries are reported plans or targets, not independently evaluated outcomes.

sources.title: Egypt Country Climate and Development Report: Executive Summary
sources.temporal_coverage: Country climate-development analysis published in 2022; includes scenarios through 2030 and 2037.
sources.methodology: Country climate-development analysis combining sector evidence, cited studies and modeled risks.
sources.limitations: Executive-summary projections rely on stated assumptions and referenced background studies.

sources.title: Egypt's Updated Nationally Determined Contributions
sources.temporal_coverage: NDC update covering 2015–2030, with national water context through 2050.
sources.methodology: Government NDC reporting national circumstances and adaptation commitments.
sources.limitations: National-level strategy; stated commitments are not evidence of delivered results.

sources.title: Project to Enhance Climate Change Adaptation in the Nile Delta and North Coast
sources.organization: Egyptian Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation
sources.temporal_coverage: Project description accessed in 2026; coastal planning scenarios extend to 2100.
sources.methodology: Official project summary of a GCF-funded coastal adaptation initiative.
sources.limitations: Describes project scope and objectives, not an independent outcome evaluation.

claims.locator: PDF p. 200 (printed p. 201), coastal vulnerability section.
claims.paraphrase: The report says Rosetta's coastal salinity rose from 27% in 1964 to above 29% by 2015, degrading cultivated land and freshwater; it links the pressure to reduced Nile Delta crop yields and food security.
claims.limitations: The report attributes the trend to cited studies; its periods are historical.

claims.paraphrase: The government reports modern surface irrigation across 4 million feddans, targeting 20% greater water efficiency; drought-, salinity- and heat-tolerant crops and Northern Delta land adaptation are also being implemented.
claims.limitations: The reported efficiency is a target; the report does not independently evaluate results.

claims.paraphrase: The report records that severe flooding in 2010 displaced thousands and damaged more than 4,000 houses; its cited historical account also notes a deadly Cairo rockslide in 2009.
claims.limitations: These are dated national report figures, not a current displacement estimate.

claims.paraphrase: The World Bank estimates over 80% of residents in Egypt's 14 major cities are exposed to at least one major climate risk; the Nile Delta is about one metre above mean sea level.
claims.limitations: The 2022 executive summary gives a city aggregate, not city-by-city rates.

claims.paraphrase: The report says poor urban residents are more likely to live on hazardous sites or in slums, face higher pollution and congestion, and lack assets or skills to cope with shocks.
claims.limitations: The source describes national patterns rather than named neighborhoods.

claims.paraphrase: The report projects that lower Nile inflows could reduce irrigated land by 22%, output per irrigated hectare by 11% and agricultural employment by 9%; its extreme-water-scarcity estimate is 2033 if resources and population trends persist.
claims.scenario: The summary states the water-scarcity assumption but does not identify a climate scenario for these figures.
claims.limitations: Scenario-dependent estimates in a 2022 executive summary.

claims.paraphrase: The 2023 NDC reports that 95% of Egypt's population lives in the Nile Valley and Delta; it records 55.5 BCM annual Nile supply against estimated needs of 114 BCM and a 97% external renewable-water dependency ratio.
institutions: Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation
claims.limitations: Figures are the dated national context presented in the 2023 NDC.

claims.paraphrase: The ministry describes GCF-backed nature-based protection for 69 km across Kafr El-Sheikh, Beheira, Port Said, Dakahlia and New Damietta, alongside a planned integrated-management strategy for 1,200 km of Mediterranean coast.
claims.scenario: The strategic plan assesses sea-level impacts on groundwater and sedimentation under scenarios to 2100.
institutions: Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation
Egyptian General Authority for Shore Protection
claims.limitations: The webpage reports project scope and plans, not completed protection outcomes.

claims.paraphrase: The coastal project also proposes small livelihood pilots with civil-society and research partners, including greenhouses and fishing-net support for local residents and small farmers.
institutions: Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation
claims.limitations: These are stated project activities; the page reports no outcome measurement.

search_audit.outcome: Searches did not locate a country-specific primary passage establishing a climate-to-conflict pathway; no such link is claimed.

search_audit.outcome: Searches did not find a source-stated conflict constraint on climate exposure or adaptation in the inspected country sources.

search_audit.query: Egypt Nile Delta coastal adaptation nature based solutions GCF local farmers project resilience capacity
search_audit.outcome: The ministry and BTR report coastal protection, irrigation, crop adaptation and water-management actions; project goals remain distinct from evaluated outcomes.

gaps: Searches found no direct country-specific evidence linking climate hazards to armed conflict or showing conflict itself blocking climate adaptation.
Some BTR adaptation figures are planned targets or government-reported implementation without an independent outcome assessment; the 2022 CCDR remains a dated executive-summary baseline.
Egypt's latest NDC/BTR update after the 2025 BTR was not verified in this extraction.
